# saferm\-notify

```go
import "github.com/shdeen/saferm/cmd/saferm-notify"
```

Command saferm\-notify runs SafeRM Notify, the optional background program that shows notifications for actions awaiting the user's approval.

## Constants

<a name="notRunningExitCode"></a>notRunningExitCode is the exit code of a \-\-quit launch that found no running SafeRM Notify.

```go
const notRunningExitCode = 2
```

<a name="notificationNameKey"></a>notificationNameKey selects the name that SafeRM Notify uses as its application name and as the title of its native dialogs.

```go
const notificationNameKey = "notification.appName"
```

<a name="reviewCategory"></a>reviewCategory identifies the notification category that offers the Approve, Deny, and Review responses.

```go
const reviewCategory = "saferm-review"
```

## func activate

func activate(data application.SecondInstanceData)

disposeNotification submits a notification decision and presents any required linked question. Only the Yes callback submits a fresh confirmed request.

<a name="main"></a>
## func main

```go
func main()
```

main runs SafeRM Notify and exits with the exit code that it returns. On failure, it logs the error and exits with status 1.

<a name="requestNotification"></a>
## func requestNotification

```go
func requestNotification(action *store.Action) notifications.NotificationOptions
```

requestNotification builds the review notification for an action. The title gives the operation type and the base name of the source, and the body names the requester when the action has one.

<a name="runNotifier"></a>
## func runNotifier

```go
func runNotifier() (int, error)
```

runNotifier runs SafeRM Notify until it quits and returns the exit code for the process. A launch while another SafeRM Notify is running is handed to the running one, which quits when the launch passed \-\-quit. A \-\-quit launch that finds no running SafeRM Notify returns notRunningExitCode without running.

<a name="Service"></a>
## type Service

Service shows a notification for each pending action that is pushed to SafeRM Notify, and carries out the response chosen on that notification.

```go
type Service struct {
    // notifications is the native notification service.
    notifications *notifications.NotificationService
    // listener receives the pushed action IDs. It is nil until startup opens it.
    listener *notify.Listener
    // workers tracks the goroutine that receives from the listener.
    workers sync.WaitGroup
}
```

<a name="Service.ServiceShutdown"></a>
### func \(\*Service\) ServiceShutdown

```go
func (service *Service) ServiceShutdown() error
```

ServiceShutdown closes the listener and waits for the receiving goroutine to exit.

<a name="Service.ServiceStartup"></a>
### func \(\*Service\) ServiceStartup

```go
func (service *Service) ServiceStartup(ctx context.Context, _ application.ServiceOptions) error
```

ServiceStartup prepares SafeRM Notify when the application starts:

- registers the response handler and the notification category for reviews
- requests permission to show notifications
- opens the listener through notify.Listen and starts receiving from it

It returns an error only when the home directory cannot be determined. It logs any other failure and returns nil; a failure to register the category or to open the listener also ends the preparation there.

<a name="Service.receive"></a>
### func \(\*Service\) receive

```go
func (service *Service) receive(ctx context.Context)
```

receive shows a review notification for each action ID that arrives on the listener, until the listener closes. It skips an action that is no longer pending and logs every failure.

<a name="Service.respond"></a>
### func \(\*Service\) respond

```go
func (*Service) respond(result notifications.NotificationResult)
```

respond carries out the response chosen on a review notification. Approve and Deny dispose of the action through saferm.Run, asking for linked consent when required. Review, or a click on the notification itself, opens the action in the GUI through desktop.Review. A failure is logged and shown in a native error dialog.
